t: You're on Prince of Wales Drive, a street in Battersea, in the borough of Wandsworth. It runs along the southern edge of Battersea Park. The street's name refers to Edward the Seventh, who held the title Prince of Wales before he became King of the United Kingdom in January 1901. He reigned until his death in 1910. So the name is a reminder of the man before the crown, attached to a road beside one of south London's best known parks.
